bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the user profile Description field: a crafted/tampered Description value is persisted, read back as profile data, passed only through Ban::filterWord and Emoticon::init (neither provides the required HTML-context XSS neutralization), assigned through nl2br to the template variable, and emitted by the profile template as {description}. Visiting the poisoned profile can therefore execute attacker-controlled JavaScript in the viewer's browser; the disclosed reproduction used the admin Users -> Browse -> Edit workflow and an intercepted/decoded request to bypass client-side encoding.
flaw_origin: Initial public repository import: root commit 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897 already contains the unsafe Description render pipeline. Later commits only migrated or restyled that same sink until the 2026 fix; no earlier public parent exists to inspect.
ai_marker: none: `git cat-file -p 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897` shows author and committer `Pierre-Henry Soria <hizup.com@hotmail.com>` at Unix time 1362183963 (-0500) and message `Initial commit`; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: Advisory bundle for CVE-2025-63644 / GHSA-657c-wxg6-jmqv identifies stored XSS in pH7-Social-Dating-CMS 17.9.1's profile Description field and records the Composer range `<= 17.9.1` with no declared first-patched version. The supplied disclosure at https://medium.com/@rudranshsinghrajpurohit/cve-2025-63644-stored-cross-site-scripting-xss-vulnerability-in-ph7-social-dating-cms-23ed0e7eb853 documents the admin edit, intercepted/decoded request, persistence, revisit, and JavaScript execution path.

At the affected tag, `git grep -n -E 'Emoticon::init\(Ban::filterWord|view->description = nl2br|\{description\}' v17.9.1 -- _protected/app/includes/classes/ProfileBaseController.php _protected/app/system/modules/user/controllers/ProfileController.php _protected/app/system/modules/user/views/base/tpl/profile/index.tpl` returns ProfileBaseController.php:303 (`Emoticon::init(Ban::filterWord($oFields->description))`), ProfileController.php:126 (`$this->view->description = nl2br($aData['description'])`), and index.tpl:317 (`{description}`). `git show v17.9.1:_protected/app/system/modules/user/forms/processing/EditFormProcess.php` also shows Description being updated from the HTTP POST in `updateDynamicFields`; the disclosure demonstrates a request-tampering bypass of the application-side encoding/cleaning.

Direct root-tree verification with `git grep -n -E 'Emoticon::init\(Ban::filterWord|view->description = nl2br|\{description\}' 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897 -- _protected/app/system/modules/user/controllers/ProfileController.php _protected/app/system/modules/user/views/base/tpl/profile/index.tpl` returns the unsafe description transform at ProfileController.php:95, assignment through `nl2br` at line 169, and raw `{description}` template emission at index.tpl:97. Thus the vulnerable lifecycle is already complete in the root commit.

The history cross-check is reproducible with `git log -L 94,94:_protected/app/system/modules/user/controllers/ProfileController.php 6ec03102ed65f30652fcfa81dc2b13f9d12f5543^`: it reaches root commit 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897, then shows 8061ffd79ae219f1ef29d8f39c2fabca8eae75c2 merely changing the data source from `$oUser->description` to `$oFields->description`. `git log -S'Emoticon::init(Ban::filterWord($oUser->description))' -- _protected/app/system/modules/user/controllers/ProfileController.php` independently returns the root introduction and the 8061ffd migration.

The later migration is not a BIC: `git log -S'Emoticon::init(Ban::filterWord($oFields->description))' -- _protected/app/system/modules/user/controllers/ProfileController.php _protected/app/includes/classes/ProfileBaseController.php` shows 8061ffd79ae219f1ef29d8f39c2fabca8eae75c2, deletion during DRY refactor 815296e16e27cdb3e928a56b0c20cf1e38e99c98, re-addition in extracted base controller 897eae4814d079a0e1ccaf81d69bf9f36738e53d, and final removal by the fix. `git log -L 303,303:_protected/app/includes/classes/ProfileBaseController.php 5aa6f489a2f8634489cb3fcd8355633bf72c3627` likewise ends at the 897eae extraction, so following the pre-extraction file is required to reach the true origin.

Parent absence is direct, not inferred: `git rev-list --parents -n 1 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897` prints only `19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897`. The root's `_protected/framework/Core/Kernel.class.php` declares `SOFTWARE_VERSION = '0.8.6'`, establishing that the unsafe sink is present at the first public version boundary.

`git show --format=fuller --patch 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a -- _protected/app/includes/classes/ProfileBaseController.php` shows a one-parent direct fix (parent 5aa6f489a2f8634489cb3fcd8355633bf72c3627): it imports `PH7\Framework\Security\Validate\Filter`, replaces the unsafe Description expression with `sanitizeDescription`, and implements `Emoticon::init((new Filter)->xssClean(Ban::filterWord($sDescription)))`. The commit subject explicitly says it sanitizes description input to prevent XSS.

Release boundary is source-verified: the same grep against v18.2.0 returns the old unsafe expression at ProfileBaseController.php:303, while v18.3.0 returns `sanitizeDescription` and `xssClean` at lines 304/319/321. `git tag --contains 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a` starts at v18.3.0 (then v18.4.0 and later), and does not list v18.2.0. The fix commit itself still declares development version 18.2.0, so v18.3.0 is the first tagged release containing the fix. The advisory's exploit is specifically established for 17.9.1; Git shows the same unsafe sink continuously from the 0.8.6 root through tagged v18.2.0.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 19cd665c32812f4d7d7ddef4b947d25344631897` contains a normal human author/committer identity, 2013 timestamps, and only `Initial commit`; no AI co-author/generated-with trailer or bot identity is present. No later refactor or fix metadata was used for the AI verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is an unsafe stored-data-to-HTML rendering pipeline, not the later location of one line. Following both `git log -L` and `git log -S` across the 2013 field-source migration and 2018 DRY extraction proves that 8061ffd79ae219f1ef29d8f39c2fabca8eae75c2, 815296e16e27cdb3e928a56b0c20cf1e38e99c98, and 897eae4814d079a0e1ccaf81d69bf9f36738e53d are moves/refactors, while the parentless 2013 root already implements database-backed Description rendering without adequate output sanitization. That root commit is therefore the smallest public-history BIC; it is an initial import rather than a decomposable squash. The one-parent 2026 commit 87fa7ae2e55aea374677b9a15b77338b9dfce98a directly closes the sink with Filter::xssClean and first ships in v18.3.0. Because the only permitted AI evidence is the BIC commit object, whose human identity/message has no AI or bot marker and predates modern coding assistants, the correct verdict is NOT_AI.
